messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), water’s freezing (melting) point is **slightly below 0 °C** – roughly **–2 °C**.  

This is because the melting curve of water lies just above the triple‑point line (6.112 kPa, –0.01 °C). As pressure increases from the triple point, the melting temperature rises, but at 10 kPa it is still only a couple of degrees below the standard 0 °C freezing point.
